author: reek
body: The shapes that lower to a single LIR block of straight-line `LiBin` arithmetic: `diff` lowers to `b0: v2 = sub v0 v1 => v2`, `addup` to `b0: v3 = add v0 v1; v4 = add v3 v2 => v4`, `poly` to `b0: v1 = mul v0 v0; v2 = add v1 v0 => v2`.

author: reek
body: This is the second construct the ARM64 LIR selector claims (`codex/plugs/arm64/Arm64Lir.codex`) and the first that consumes the register assignment, so on that backend these definitions are emitted by a different code path from every other function in the file, and their bytes depend on what the allocator answered. x86-64 compiles them the way it always did, which is what makes the two answers comparable.

author: reek
body: `via-call` exists so the answers are not read only from the definitions themselves: it calls them, which means the function offsets and arities the selector registers have to be right for an ordinary call to land, and the caller is a tree-emitted function reading a selector-emitted one.
